cards.f: How long should the summary take in the exam?
Timing plan: first 2 minutes of the summary?
cards.b: Read the question and underline the focus. Is it one part or two?
Read Text B and highlight relevant ideas only.
Plan: list ideas in 2-4 words of your own, remove repeats and examples, group related points.
Write the summary from the plan, once (no draft and neat copy).
Count words, replace lifted key words, check spelling and full stops.

cards.f: How many creditable ideas does Text B usually have?
cards.b: About 10-15. If your plan has only 4-5, reread for ideas hidden in examples.

cards.f: Why plan in notes and write once?
cards.b: Writing a draft then a neat copy wastes time you do not have.

cards.f: Concise pattern: list in one sentence.
cards.b: e.g. 'Night workers often suffer from poor sleep, weight gain and heart problems.'
e.g. 'Because they sleep in the day, they see less of their families.'
e.g. 'Although better paid, the work isolates them.'
'Another thing that the text says is that...' (7 wasted words).

cards.f: What if the focus has two parts (reasons for... and problems with...)?
cards.b: You need both parts. Include ideas for each.

cards.f: Should you copy a quotation from a person in the text?
cards.b: No. Rephrase the point in your own words.

cards.f: What should you do with the best practice resource?
cards.b: Use an unseen real 0500 Paper 1 summary and its official mark scheme, then mark yourself.

gaps.s: The summary should take about ___ minutes in the exam.
The summary limit is no more than ___ words.
Most Text B passages have roughly 10 to ___ creditable ideas.
In the exam you should plan in notes and write ___ , not draft then copy neatly.
Top level writing marks reward answers that are concise and in ___ words throughout.
Final minutes should be used to ___ your words.
A summary should not include an ___ such as 'This text is about...'.
If the question asks for benefits, you should leave out ___.

short.q: Explain why the focus must be underlined first. [2]
short.model: It tells you which ideas are relevant, so you only select material that answers the question.

short.q: Shorten: 'Another thing the text says is that night workers often have poor sleep, and also weight gain.' [2]
short.model: Night workers often suffer poor sleep and weight gain.

short.q: Why is writing a draft and a neat copy a mistake in the summary? [2]
short.model: It uses up time. Plan in notes and write once so you can count words and check.

short.q: Your plan has only four ideas. What should you do? [2]
short.model: Reread Text B because you are probably missing ideas inside examples. Aim for 10-15 ideas.

short.q: State what the top level for reading and writing needs. [3]
short.model: Reading: wide range of relevant ideas, clearly understood. Writing: concise, well organised, own words throughout.
